description: Language-neutral conformance corpus for the AID runtimes. One case per behaviour: `id` names it, `op` selects the operation, `input` is the language-neutral fixture and `expect` is the observable outcome. A runner maps `input` onto its own runtime's types, computes `observed` and compares. Floating-point results are rounded to 6 decimal places so that a case pins a behaviour rather than the last bit of one implementation's summation order; non-finite values are the strings "inf", "-inf" and "nan" because JSON has no representation for them. Nothing here is language-specific: no case names a module, a function or a type from either runtime. A case may carry `runtimes`, the list of runtimes it applies to (absent means all of them), and must then carry a non-empty `reason` unless it applies to every runtime. A runtime that is named must implement the case's `op` -- a scope narrows who is checked, never what is. Each runner reports a case it does not apply as `scoped-out` with that reason rather than omitting it, so both runtimes' verdict artefacts list the same ids and a comparison never claims agreement on a case it did not evaluate.

cases.description: The critical value is taken from the tabulated levels at or below alpha, so an untabulated alpha rounds to the next stricter level and anything stricter than the table gets the strictest value.
The regression statistic divides the delta by the standard error of the difference of two means, so both spreads contribute: the same drop is judged against the noise in the run and in the baseline.
